portInfo.description: Kailua-Kona Wharf is managed by Hawaiʻi’s Department of Land and Natural Resources Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation (DOBOR), which lists it as a cruise ship port with an offshore mooring area, a 16-foot-wide commercial ramp, three loading/unloading areas, vessel washdown, and a comfort station with outside showers. DOBOR publishes dedicated forms for ground-transportation operators and free shuttles coordinating cruise-ship passenger transport from Kailua Pier. Contact phone (808) 327-3685; email dlnr.bd.kailua-konapier@hawaii.gov; mailing address at Honokohau Small Boat Harbor. Commercial cargo-harbour scheduling for the State’s deep-draft ports is separate (Hawaii.PortCall.Com under HDOT); Kailua Pier’s cruise tender operation is the DOBOR facility evidenced here.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Treat Kona as a tender-first day — a late morning swell can erase a snorkel window even when the calendar looks long.
